title: Abstract Ethical Concepts with Neuter Lo

sections.content:
You know neuter *lo* + masculine singular adjective (*lo bueno*, *lo malo*, *lo importante*, *lo difícil*) from B1 Unit 40, where you also met it before a past participle and in *lo bueno de vivir en el centro*. In philosophy and ethics, neuter *lo* becomes the primary tool for turning moral qualities and categories into abstract concepts:

• ***Lo* + ethical/logical adjective**: names a moral or philosophical category (*lo justo*, *lo verdadero*, *lo racional*, *lo lícito*, *lo subjetivo*). The adjective is always masculine singular, even when paired with a feminine noun later in the sentence.
• ***Lo* + past participle**: names what is required, allowed, or agreed (*lo debido*, *lo permitido*, *lo acordado*).
• ***Lo* + adjective + *de* + noun**: isolates a specific facet of a dilemma (*Lo paradójico del dilema es que ambas opciones tienen coste moral*).

sections.title: Neuter lo in philosophical prose
rows: La filosofía distingue entre lo verdadero y lo útil.
Philosophy distinguishes between what is true and what is useful.
No todo lo lícito coincide con lo moral.
Not everything permissible coincides with what is moral.
Debemos separar lo racional de lo subjetivo.
We must separate what is rational from what is subjective.
Lo paradójico del caso reside en sus consecuencias.
What is paradoxical about the case lies in its consequences.

items.spanish: En filosofía práctica, distinguir lo justo de lo simplemente útil es el primer paso del debate.
items.english: In practical philosophy, distinguishing what is just from what is merely useful is the first step of the debate.

items.spanish: Cumplir lo acordado forma parte de lo debido en cualquier relación de confianza.
items.english: Keeping what was agreed is part of what is owed in any relationship of trust.

items.spanish: Lo paradójico de muchos dilemas morales es que dos principios válidos chocan entre sí.
items.english: What is paradoxical about many moral dilemmas is that two valid principles clash with each other.

items.spanish: Conviene no confundir lo subjetivo con lo arbitrario cuando se busca un criterio racional.
items.english: It is wise not to confuse what is subjective with what is arbitrary when seeking a rational criterion.

sections.content: Never make the adjective after neuter *lo* agree in gender or number with a following noun: say *Lo complejo de estas normas* (never `*La compleja de estas normas*` or `*Los complejos de estas normas*`). And remember that *lo* never precedes a plain noun (`*lo dilema*` is wrong).
